[b]The White Sea Caucus[/b]

Minister Ostman, together with the members of the hawkish "White Sea Caucus" of the House Radicals, would enact a six-point response to Queen Mij Drs's offers of diplomatic dialogue, once again reiterating that the island of Austmark now constitutes, together with its exclusive economic zone, the newest territorial extent of both the State of Norrhollow and the Commonwealth of High Albany. In a session before the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, Ostman and other key Radical allies reiterate its previous points without showing any evidence of compromise:

[list][b]Ostman's Six Points[/b]

[*]The island of Austmark is a fundamental territory of the Commonwealth of High Albany.

[*]Austmark's occupation and annexation were done in accordance with democratic instruments.

[*]Austmark's occupation and annexation did not impede the life, liberty, or property of any living persons, Thrømm or Albic, and were undertaken with the highest consideration for potential ecological impacts.

[*]Speculation as to Austmark's role as a forward operating base (FOB) designed to target the sovereignty of the Thýven is baseless and steeped in anti-Albic xenophobia.

[*]As evidenced by internal investigations, the Thrømm maintain no basis for laying claim to Austmark, nor did later field work by Albic officers reveal any evidence of Thrømm settlements in the area, whether in the form of documents or archaelogical evidence.

[*]Thýven is the sole originator of political tensions concerning Austmark Island, which High Albany is merely striving to defend.

[/list]

The six points would be physically delivered to the Albic embassy in Tharkønn by the Albic ambassador to Thýven, David Aakjaer, stamped with the seal of the Commonwealth. Another document attached would include a list of Albic dignitaries that have supported the six points, the chief of which would be Minister Ostman. Other notable signatures would include centrist Moderates like Governor Eske Fjällstra of Norrhollow and Lieutenant Governor Honor Almstedt, as well as all representatives under the White Sea Caucus.

Opposition to the White Sea Caucus would manifest chiefly in the form of the dovish factions of the Radical Party and some isolationist elements within the Moderate Party, both of whom would criticize Minister Ostman's actions as extend beyond her executive mandate. Though, with public opinion strongly in favor of the White Sea Caucus, these pro-compromise politicians would remain silent for now, waiting patiently for Thýven's response to the six points.
